prioritize: Reframe angles that challenge unspoken assumptions (low confidence: small sample, top-performing format so far, heavily influenced by one 88.67% outlier)
Declarative statement hooks centered on quiet emotional realities (low-to-medium confidence: directional lead over direct accusation hooks, small sample)
Observations exploring private emotional endurance, quiet grieving, and boundary shifts
reduce: Direct accusation hooks (directional signal only: n=2, ~30.5% retention, early drop-off noted in audit)
Abstract truth drops lacking concrete situational anchors (small sample, directional only)

cooldowns.reason: Direct accusation hooks ('You're still asking...', 'They Googled you...') averaged ~30.5% retention on a very small sample with sharp early drop-off. Short cooldown to test the signal, not a permanent ban; also conflicts with the brand rule against judgmental tone toward the viewer.

research.notes: With 12 eligible videos and view counts of roughly 50-200, all findings are directional, not statistically reliable. Reframe and declarative hooks lead so far, but the top result (88.67% on 'Moving on fast means you cared QUIETLY') is a single outlier. Treat as hypotheses to keep testing, not settled rules.

prioritize: Declarative statement hooks that voice an internal conflict without assigning blame
Resonant loopback lines in the final 5 seconds to encourage completion and replay value
Tight 30-45 second narrative structures with clear psychological progression (tension -> reframe -> quiet resolution), ending on empowerment rather than pity
reduce: Confrontational opening lines targeting viewer insecurity directly
Broad existential statements that fail to introduce an identifiable everyday anchor in the first 3 seconds
cta_patterns: Soft observation loops over aggressive engagement asks; avoid banned phrases and generic self-help reminders
script.word_count_signal: Maintain the 55-70 word target (optimizing for 30-45 second run time at deliberate, unhurried pacing).

prioritize: Grounded, specific visual metaphors tied directly to the spoken line (e.g., search queries, stacked documents, quiet physical boundaries)
A more specific, attention-catching opening visual in the first 1.5-2 seconds, while keeping the muted, cinematic brand aesthetic
Subtle shifts toward warmer or resolving visuals on loopback statements
reduce: Overly generic stock b-roll (empty oceanic chairs, padlocks, ambiguous silhouettes gazing out windows) that disconnects from the voiceover
Static shots held longer than 3 seconds during the mid-video narrative bridge
visuals.thumbnail_signal: Text-driven, minimal imagery prioritizing emotional clarity; follow the primary variant rule (never A, default B, prefer C if thumbnail text passes the non-clinical check) and avoid all banned thumbnail words.

metadata.title_signal: Declarative, observation-led titles (e.g. 'Moving on fast means you cared QUIETLY') are leading so far over confrontational curiosity gaps; sample is small, so keep testing.
metadata.description_signal: Keep descriptions grounded in accurate, searchable reflections of the central reframe without clinical buzzwords or banned phrases.
prioritize: Declarative reframe titles that articulate a recognizable private feeling
Selective capitalization of a single pivotal word (e.g., QUIETLY) to anchor feed scanning; use sparingly so it does not become a formula
reduce: Second-person accusatory titles ('They Googled you', 'You're still asking for permission')

prioritize: Empathetic, steady, contemplative cadence with distinct micro-pauses before reframe revelations
Consistent audio mix levels with clean separation between voiceover and ambient, understated score
voice.notes: Voiceover quality is the channel's strongest audited asset across performance tiers. Ensure pacing is dictated by punctuation in scripts rather than accelerated delivery.

prioritize: Variant B default layout with clean typography
Variant C when text is brief, punchy, and completely free of clinical terminology

this_week.hypothesis: Opening with an immediate physical action or grounded object metaphor (rather than a solitary person gazing) will improve early retention on declarative hooks compared with recent generic openers.
Ending the script on a close inversion of the opening hook may improve completion and replay; evaluate directionally given the small sample.

wildcard_slots.hypothesis: Featuring the raccoon mascot as a subtle, thoughtful environmental observer (not cute or goofy) in an early and late scene may strengthen brand recognition without compromising the contemplative tone.
